claims.action: Hold first lot after every wheat campaign until an ELISA (R5) test of finished product reads < 10 ppm; or buy a dedicated small blender for the 3 wheat mixes (about $40-60k) and remove the risk.
claims.status: AT RISK: needs validated clean + finished-product test

sanitary.sanitary: 304/316 SS contact parts, polished; intensifier bar optional
sanitary SS, spout access chamber with dust seal
clean-out door, flush discharge valve, load cells option (documented), Ra <= 0.8 um contact
stainless finish version; reject to locked container
inflatable spout seal, vent to DC-310
sanitary, full clean-out by removing the screw
SS auger and funnel, magnetic funnel quick release (documented)

nfpa: NFPA 652 dust hazard analysis (DHA) before ordering DC-310; send Kst/Pmax and MIE samples of the 3 highest-volume blends to a test lab.
NFPA 61 (agricultural/food dusts): collector outside the building, explosion vent directed away from people, isolation flap valve on the inlet duct.
Ducts sized for >= 4,000 ft/min transport velocity; no horizontal duct runs where avoidable; cleanouts every 3 m.
Bond and ground every conveying element (< 10 ohm); flexible screws and FIBC spouts use Type C bags or grounded Type B with a grounding clamp on BB-302, BU-401 and BU-502.
Housekeeping: dust layer on any surface over 1/32 in (0.8 mm) triggers cleaning; vacuum only with a Class II Div 2 rated vacuum (Nilfisk), never compressed air.
Electrical in blending and weigh rooms: Class II Div 2 Group G unless the DHA shows otherwise; panels CP-300/CP-400 sit outside the exposed-product rooms.

haccp.step: Metal detection MD-305 (after sifter, before bulk bag)
haccp.hazard: Physical: metal fragments from raw spice or equipment wear
haccp.limit: No blend passes containing Fe >= 1.5 mm, non-Fe >= 2.0 mm, 316 SS >= 2.5 mm spheres (confirm at FAT with the product effect)
haccp.monitor: Test wands through the aperture at start, every 2 h, at end and after any stop; reject-confirm sensor and locked reject bin
haccp.correct: Failed test: hold all blend since the last good test, re-run it through MD-305, find the cause, record
haccp.verify: QA reviews records daily; annual validation by Mettler-Toledo
haccp.records: MES batch record (md_rejects), MD-305 test log

haccp.ccp: CCP-2 (allergen, if the HACCP team classifies it as a CCP)
haccp.step: Allergen changeover after the wheat campaign
haccp.hazard: Chemical/allergen: wheat gluten cross-contact into gluten-free seasonings
haccp.limit: Gluten swab < 10 ppm at every listed point; first allergen-free lot < 10 ppm (ELISA R5)
haccp.monitor: Swabs after the wet clean; finished-product test of the first lot
haccp.correct: Re-clean and re-swab; hold and test lots; no gluten-free claim on a failed lot
haccp.records: SSOP log, swab results, ELISA certificate in MES

ssop.task: Dry clean pack line A contact parts
ssop.method: vacuum (Nilfisk Class II), dry brush (Vikan color-coded), wipe
ssop.verify: visual + ATP swab < 150 RLU on 3 points

ssop.task: Blender sequence purge between allergen-free formulas
ssop.method: run blender empty, brush ribbons, vacuum valve, purge with 25 kg salt (reused as carrier salt)

ssop.task: Full dry clean of the blending train
ssop.method: open RB-303 cover (locked out), scrape and vacuum; sifter screen out; magnet wiped

ssop.when: Friday after the wheat campaign (outside production minutes)
ssop.method: disassemble per the joints on ASM-001; wash, sanitize (quat, no-rinse), dry with forced air for 12 h
ssop.verify: gluten swabs < 10 ppm; first Monday lot ELISA

ssop.when: after the wheat campaign on B
ssop.method: same as above for BU-502 and NW-501

prerequisites: Supplier approval with COA per lot; spices bought steam-treated or ETO-free validated (Salmonella log reduction by the supplier) because the plant has no kill step.
Raw material micro: Salmonella negative in 375 g, per COA; skip-lot verification testing.
Sifter SC-304 with a 12 mesh screen and the DH-102 magnet: screens checked for damage each shift (prerequisite, not a CCP).
Net contents: CW-409 rejects every unit under declared (site rule); NIST HB 133 lot check in the MES.
Label control: first-off UPC and lot code check signed in the MES before the line can run; label rolls stored per SKU.
Pest control, glass and brittle plastic register, foreign-material policy, hygiene vestibule with hand wash and boot wash into Z3.
